body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need you to write about 40 lines for ONE scene at a time. Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The scene

Ezmerelda d'Avenir is a young Vistana monster hunter (long dark coat, rapier, a small crossbow with silver-headed bolts, a spyglass, and an oak-and-steel brace below her right knee where a werewolf took her leg). She was trained by Rudolph van Richten, the legendary monster hunter, who walked into the mists twelve years ago to die alone and has been calling himself Rictavio ever since: a loud half-elf showman in a scarlet coat and a hat of feathers who lodges at the Blue Water Inn in the town of Vallaki and keeps a gaudy crimson carnival wagon in the inn's stable yard that nobody may open. (A great cat is caged in it; the horses in the stable hate it. He hides his real self from the vampire lord Strahd, who would kill him.) Rudolph is really an exhausted, sharp old man with burn-scarred hands who has lost nearly everyone he taught and does not want her to be the next.

The player's party met Ezmerelda camped at Rudolph's tower on Lake Baratok, where his ward (keyed to her alone) had thrown her into the lake. They told her where he was. She said: "Feathers? Tell me there are feathers. No, don't. I'll see for myself. I'm leaving tonight." Now she has come to Vallaki and is waiting in the stable yard at the back of the inn, by his locked wagon, and the party finds her there.

Her fear (the voice bible's secret, never stated flatly): being too late again, and being left behind again. She has not knocked because she is not sure what she will say to him, or whether he wants to be found. She scouted the taproom through the window, saw a man in feathers standing on a chair addressing nobody in particular, and had to sit down. The yard is private (nobody else is in it). The inn is kept by the Martikov family; there are horses in stalls, hay bales, a lantern by the wagon steps, and the wagon's door is padlocked.

Rudolph's room at the inn has a rack of costumes, a washstand with a stage moustache on it, and a lute. In the unmasked version of him he is "low, clipped, precise"; as Rictavio he is bombast and alliteration. He keeps the costume on in public even after the party knows (the town must not suspect); only the voice changes. The wagon's door has a hair across the lock, a habit of his that she would know.

What the lines are for. Nodes, in the order the player meets them:

1. The party enters the yard and Ezmerelda greets them (first time).
2. A menu: bring him out to her / ask why she hasn't gone in / leave.
3. The reunion, when the party brings Rudolph out to her. It has TWO openings (he already knows the party knows who he is; or he does not and arrives in his showman act) and then ONE shared exchange. Her pet test to strangers is "Say something a vampire wouldn't say." Please build the exchange so that she uses that line on him and his answer is the emotional centre (something true and not at all showman-like, such as an apology). It must end like the tower's reunion did: she hits him on the arm, hard, and he lets her. Do not copy the tower's reunion lines (listed below); invent new beats. The great cat in the wagon may react once for a laugh. A variant node is used only if the party had promised to keep his secret and told her anyway: he says so, she takes the blame ("I got it out of them").
4. After the reunion she gives the party a gift (silver-headed bolts, holy water, a healing potion, and a coat of glamoured armour that can look like a ball gown or a beggar's coat). Two lines, neutral about where she is.
5. Later visits to her in the yard: a short hub (how is Rudolph, hunt with us, goodbye) and a joining speech (she joins the party as a companion).
6. Separately: if the showman has already left Vallaki by the time she arrives (he went home to his tower, or he left with the party), she goes back to her camp at Lake Baratok and the party finds her there instead. Short, with a variant.

## The nodes I need (line counts are targets; one line = 1-2 short sentences)

yard_first: Narrator x2 (the stable yard; a woman in a long dark coat sitting on a hay bale across from a crimson wagon, a crossbow across her knee, who has plainly been there a long time), Ezmerelda x3 (greets you; says she has seen him and that there are feathers; why she is sitting here and not in the taproom)
yard_again: Ezmerelda x1 (the party comes back before the reunion; she has not moved)
yard_why: Ezmerelda x2 (an honest answer to "why haven't you gone in?"; her fear shown through a joke, not stated)
yard_leave: Ezmerelda x1 (goodbye to the party, as they leave her there)
reunion_unmasked: Narrator x1, Rictavio x2 (he knows the party knows who he is, comes out into the yard at the party's word; he stops in the doorway when he sees her; low and clipped, one line of dread and one of surrender)
reunion_costume: Narrator x1, Rictavio x2 (he does not know; he comes out mid-flourish in his showman act and the act dies in his mouth when he sees her)
reunion_scene: Ezmerelda x4, Rictavio x4, Narrator x1 (the shared exchange, in whatever order is best; she uses "Say something a vampire wouldn't say"; he answers truthfully; the last beat is Narrator: she hits him on the arm, hard, and he lets her - write that Narrator line freshly, not copied)
reunion_promise: Rictavio x1, Ezmerelda x1 (only if the party had promised him to keep his secret; he reproaches them; she takes the blame)
reunion_end: Rictavio x1 (to the party, gruff thanks in his unmasked voice), Ezmerelda x1 (to the party, dry)
gift: Ezmerelda x2 (a hunter's gift: bolts, holy water, a potion, then the coat; neutral, so it reads right in the yard or elsewhere)
yard_after: Ezmerelda x2 (the hub after the reunion: she is staying near him for now; her state of mind)
yard_rudolph: Ezmerelda x2 (an answer to "How is Rudolph?": she complains about him with love)
join: Ezmerelda x2 (she agrees to hunt with the party; neutral about where she is, since it is also used on a road at night)
shore_gone: Narrator x1, Ezmerelda x3 (the party finds her back at her camp on the shore of Lake Baratok; she went to Vallaki and he was gone from the inn; she suspects he went home to his tower and is hiding in it again; she tells the party to go in and tell him she is outside, and what she will do to him)
shore_with_him: Ezmerelda x1 (the same shore scene, but Rudolph is walking with the party as a companion; one line to the party before she sees him, about the wasted walk to Vallaki)

## Option texts

Under the nodes below, also write what the party (not Ezmerelda) says, as `* text` lines, in this order, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we"), no attitude beyond the intent given:
yard_first: `* ` bring him out to her  /  `* ` ask why she hasn't gone in
yard_after: `* ` ask how Rudolph is

That is 41 lines plus 3 options.

## Ezmerelda d'Avenir - voice bible

Quick, sardonic, practical; hunter's rules delivered as jokes. Teases, then means it. Calls Van Richten "Rudolph" and treats his legend with exasperated love. Pet phrases: "Say something a vampire wouldn't." "Silver first, questions never." "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at." Funny through showman timing (she grew up in wagons that put on shows), self-mockery about her own missing parts, and her running complaint about her teacher's habits. Wants: Strahd's end; to find Rudolph and have a word with him first. Fears: being too late again; being left behind again. Secret: she isn't sure she's as brave as her reputation, and has started to think that's wisdom.

Existing Ezmerelda lines (match this register; do not repeat them):
- "Stop there. Say something a vampire wouldn't say."
- "Ezmerelda [smile]: A vampire would have said something about my eyes. Fine. Sit down before you fall in the lake."
- "Nobody with fangs has ever asked to buy silver. Not twice, anyway. Sit."
- "Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Vistani, when the wagons will have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. Right now I'm hunting one stubborn old man who taught me how, and who has locked me out of his house."
- "He's making tea. He's terrible at tea. Don't tell him; he thinks it's the only thing he's good at besides killing."
- "Feathers? Tell me there are feathers. No, don't. I'll see for myself. I'm leaving tonight."
- "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at. Rudolph says it'll kill me. Rudolph says a lot, from very far away."
- "I go first through doors. Not because I'm brave. Because I've got the leg that doesn't bleed."
- "Angels don't stitch. Whatever runs this abbey, it's been practising on people."
- "I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me 'girl'."

The tower's reunion (the version the player would see if Rudolph were at the tower instead; do NOT reuse these ideas or lines):
- Ezmerelda: "Rudolph. You're wearing feathers." Rictavio: "It's a costume. It's a very good costume." Ezmerelda: "It's a terrible costume. You look like a chicken that's been to a wedding. You keyed your ward to me." Rictavio: "Everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, Ezmerelda. You are the last. I would like you to stay the last." Ezmerelda: "Then you should have stayed alive near me, so you could keep an eye on me. That was always the deal." Narrator: "Neither of them says anything for a while. Then she hits him on the arm, hard, and he lets her."

## Rictavio / Rudolph van Richten - voice bible

As Rictavio: bombast, alliteration, audience patter, never a straight answer. Unmasked: low, clipped, precise; hard-won rules; treats the party as students he didn't ask for. Funny through the gap between the costume and the man, and by telling the truth inside a joke. Wants: Strahd's end; to stay unknown. Fears: his name reaching the castle; another protege dying in his place. Speaker name in the lines: `Rictavio` (even when unmasked).

Existing Rictavio lines (match; do not repeat):
- "Rictavio [smile]: Friends! Strangers! Strange friends! Rictavio, at your service: teller of tales, singer of songs, proprietor of the most marvellous carnival wagon in seven valleys, which none of you may look inside!"
- "Rictavio: Not that name. Not here. Rudolph van Richten made a great many enemies, and some of them have extremely long lives. Rictavio has none. I would like to keep it that way."
- "Rictavio: Keep your voice down and your back to the wall. What do you need?"
- "Rictavio: A tale! There was once a hunter who chased a monster across the whole world, and caught it, and killed it. And do you know what he found? That there was always another monster. The end. It goes better with a lute."
- "Rictavio: I keyed the ward to her because everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, and she is the last. If she can't get in, she can't follow me where I'm going."
- "Rictavio: Stay in the light where you can. And when you can't, stay together."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Ominous, dryly funny, never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level", "skill". No winks at the player. Here the Narrator may be warm: this is a reunion.
Samples:
- "The hall smells of beeswax and old smoke. Somebody kept this house beautifully, right up until they didn't."
- "By a painted wagon, a woman in a long dark coat sits fixing silver heads to crossbow bolts. Below her right knee, a brace of oak and steel; her left hand is bandaged, and she smells faintly of burnt hair."
- "She doesn't look up. She lifts a small loaded crossbow off her knee instead and points it at you."
- "The showman goes out of him like air out of a bladder. What's left is an old man, very tired and very alert, who sits down and lowers his voice."

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history beyond what is given: no new characters, no named innkeepers (the Martikovs may be mentioned only as "the innkeepers"), no new monsters, no past adventures of hers or his beyond what is in this brief. Rudolph's wagon holds a caged great cat; do not give it a name or powers. Ezmerelda never calls the party "kids" or "girl". She does not say Strahd's name in the yard (walls have ears): "the lord of this valley", "the castle", or nothing. Moods: Ezmerelda may use [smile] or [angry] (or no mood); Rictavio may use [smile], [sly], [weary] (or no mood); Narrator never has a mood.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator, Ezmerelda or Rictavio. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud by an actor: so NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Use plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. For the three option texts write them as `* text` rows under the node named for them. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

body:
Thank you, that was a good draft: the "say something a vampire wouldn't say" turn works. Same game, same characters, same format and rules as before (plain text, `~ node_name`, one line per row, `Speaker [mood]: Text`, 1-2 sentences, under 22 words, spoken aloud, plain ASCII, no stage directions inside a speaker's line, no names beyond the brief). Now I need two small redrafts and the second scene set.

## Part 1: two redrafts

Redraft A, `reunion_scene` (only the cat's moment). In your reply, "Something heavy hits the inside of the wagon door with a low, wet snarl. Even your luggage has better manners than you do." was spoken by Ezmerelda but describes the world, and the next line ("Do not tap the woodwork") then makes no sense. Give me, under `~ reunion_cat`: Narrator x1 (the great cat in the wagon reacts, from behind the closed door, to Rictavio's apology; it does not attack, speak or escape; a dry, warm beat), then Ezmerelda x1 (one dry line to him about the cat or about the apology, no stage direction inside it). It comes straight after his "I am sorry" line and before her "Twelve years..." line.

Redraft B, `shore_with_him`. She must NOT see him yet. She is bent over her bolts at her camp on the lake shore and speaks, without looking up, to the party: she walked to Vallaki and back for an empty stable yard (the innkeepers said the showman had gone), and she is in no mood for news about where he went. One line, angry, funny. After your line the game's existing scene continues with: "The woman by the wagon looks up from her bolts, sees who is walking behind you, and goes completely still." (so he is standing right behind the party, which she has not noticed).

## Part 2: three meetings on the road

Ezmerelda is a companion-in-waiting: the party has met her, but she is not travelling with them, and now and then they come across her in the middle of her own hunting. Each of the three scenes below is a short, self-contained conversation opener; after it the game shows a menu (is Rudolph well, hunt with us, goodbye), so do not end any scene on a question to the party. In every scene, Ezmerelda: (1) says something first on seeing them, in her dry voice; (2) gives her hunter's view of what lies ahead for them on this road or in this place, practical and a little funny, WITHOUT giving puzzle answers or telling them what to do in a quest; (3) lets slip one small true thing about herself that she has not said to anyone (a quiet trust moment, shown not stated: her hands, her fear of being useless, her teacher). Keep each of these three beats to one line. Narrator x2 sets the scene BEFORE she speaks (what the party sees: where she is, what she is doing, a concrete sense).

road_svalich: the Old Svalich Road at night, fog between black pines, the party coming on a woman in a long dark coat standing over a body in the road. The body is a vampire spawn (one of the lord of the valley's former victims, now his servant) and she has just staked it: the stake still stands in its chest, the corpse is already collapsing into dust and rags, and she is wiping a mallet on her coat. Spawn walk the roads at night, sent from the castle; they sleep by day. Her view of the road: whoever is sending them is sending them down this road, in ones and twos, to watch for travellers; listen for the dragging feet before you see anything.

road_berez: the drowned fields of Berez, the ruined village in the marsh south-west of Vallaki, in daylight under low cloud. The witch Baba Lysaga lives here in a hut that stands on a giant stump and walks when it likes, and scarecrows stand in the reeds around her stump; the scarecrows move when nobody is looking. Ezmerelda is in the reeds with a hatchet, chopping a scarecrow off its post. Her view: witches feed you before they hurt you; keep your hands full of something other than her food; and anything that stands in a field in a pose is not decoration here.

road_manor: the road below Argynvostholt, the ruined manor of the dead Order of the Silver Dragon on a hill above the valley. The knights are revenants (the dead who rise to settle a score and do not stop until it is settled), led by Vladimir Horngaard; pale lights move in the manor's broken windows and the beacon tower on its roof is dark. She is lying on her stomach in the heather with her spyglass, watching the windows. Her view: they are not hunting travellers on the road; walk up as guests, not as thieves, and do not draw steel on a revenant you cannot finish, since it will get up again.

road_svalich: Narrator x2, Ezmerelda x3
road_berez: Narrator x2, Ezmerelda x3
road_manor: Narrator x2, Ezmerelda x3

## Part 3: the short answers after the three scenes

The menu after any of the three scenes has these options. Write the option texts (what the party says, under 12 words, in the party's voice) and her answers:

road_rudolph_reunited: Ezmerelda x1 (answer to "How is Rudolph holding up?" when the two of them are reconciled; he is well and unbearable; neutral about where he is)
road_rudolph_waiting: Ezmerelda x1 (answer when she knows where he is - at the Blue Water Inn in Vallaki - but has not yet gone in to him; she is working up to it and goes out at night to hunt so that she does not think about it) with the option text `* ` ask whether she has spoken to him yet
road_rudolph_seeking: Ezmerelda x1 (answer when she has not yet found him at all; still looking) with the option text `* ` ask whether she has found her teacher yet
road_not_yet: Ezmerelda x1 (she is asked to hunt with the party but will not come before she has looked Rudolph in the eye; she is staying at the Blue Water Inn's stable yard in Vallaki, find her there)
road_bye: Ezmerelda x1 (a hunter's parting on the road, dry; works day or night)

That is 3 redraft lines, 15 scene lines, 5 answer lines and 2 option texts.
